rationale: Eight sources, in six subject areas, report the pattern and several state it about their own results. Where the same method is run across a size or capability ladder, the margin decreases with backbone strength: a structured spatial-reasoning method leads its category by 16.85 percent at 3B and 9.51 at 7B; a self-correction method's gains shrink on its three newest backbones, which its authors attribute to those models already self-correcting before training; and rationale supervision buys nothing in-domain for strong backbones while buying 20 to 28 points out of domain, with a language-specific model gaining least of all and the weakest general backbone gaining most. Where the ladder is a mismatch axis rather than a size axis the effect is starker: one distillation method's advantage is 1.0 point where the student is close to the teacher -- inside the spread of three other baselines -- and 13.4 where it is far below, and the strong-mismatch baseline is a model emitting 22K-token unterminated responses, so much of what is demonstrated there is repair of breakage. Crossing families rather than sizes can reverse the ordering outright: a preference method reaching 62.33 percent on a mathematics set with one 8B backbone loses to a baseline on another (23.01 against 23.51); three post-training algorithms improve one family's model on every subjective task while the other family's falls below its own reasoning baseline on three of four under all three; and a safety pipeline's utility cost lands entirely on one family, which its authors attribute to reasoning-style mismatch with the teacher rather than to the defence. There is also a floor, not only a ceiling: the same jury distillation that lifts a 12B student lowers a 4B one, a limit that source scopes around rather than states. Two consequences for reading this archive. A margin reported on one backbone should be read as evidence that an intervention does something rather than as an estimate of how much, and a ladder that is monotone in one family is not evidence of a scaling law -- one source reports exactly such a ladder (+2.46, +4.85, +12.01) and explicitly declines to call it one. And the standard control is cheap: run the second family, and report the backbone's own headroom alongside the margin.
statement: A method's reported margin is largely a property of how much headroom its backbone had: the same intervention gains most on the weakest model and shrinks, vanishes or reverses on a stronger one or on a second family — so a single-backbone result establishes the direction of an effect and not its size.
